item.title: Journal Prompts for Slowing Down: 3 Gentle Questions
item.description: Three journal prompts for slowing down, inspired by Japanese ideas like kizuki (気づき), the moment of noticing. Where am I rushing without needing to? What would one unhurried hour look like? What can wait until tomorrow? Write a few lines for each, or simply sit with one. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.

item.title: Itadakimasu (いただきます) Meaning: I Humbly Receive
item.description: Itadakimasu (いただきます) is a Japanese word meaning “I humbly receive.” Said before a meal in Japan, often as thanks to everything that made it possible. Who helped bring today's food to you? From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.

item.title: Haiku About the Harvest Moon by Kobayashi Issa, in a New Translation
item.description: A haiku by Kobayashi Issa (1763–1828): “Get me that moon!” the child cries — the harvest moon. Some wishes are too beautiful to refuse, and too big to grant. Translation our own. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.

item.title: Free Guide: 5 Days of Japanese Ideas for Everyday Calm
item.description: A free 5-day guide to Japanese ideas for everyday calm: one idea, one five-minute practice, and one question each day. A printable PDF — no pressure, no noise, just a quiet place to begin. From GLOBAL INNER DIVINE, a small studio in Japan.
